items.text: The IPC server's request, reply and routing layer is shared, so the Linux app answers commands the way Windows does.
The Linux app answers the ghoztty CLI on its own 0600 Unix socket, and a command run in one of its panes always reaches that app.
test/linux/ipc-server.sh is executable like its siblings.
test/linux/cli-send-read.sh: K7 matches type-ahead output, and the script is executable.
test/linux/cli-send-read.sh is executable like its siblings.
A script can type into a Linux pane and read back what it shows: +send-keys and +read are served by the GTK app.
Activity Monitor's Show all checkbox is greyed out when it can do nothing.
The OpenGL loader's fallback log line can no longer overrun its buffer on a long non-ASCII install path.
Closing an SSH connection now wakes its reader on Linux.
A floor fixture that never comes up now says what the app was doing.
Starting from a shell without a console no longer leaves the app's stderr pointing at its own IPC pipe.
